items.title: Central AHU ventilation
items.text: Ventilation for the building is provided by One (1) central air handling unit(s), located in roof top, equipment with outdoor-air intake and return/exhaust paths serving corridors and other public areas.

items.title: Garage exhaust with demand control
items.text: Garage ventilation is controlled by carbon monoxide sensing with demand-based exhaust fan operation. This approach helps reduce fan runtime during low-occupancy periods.

items.title: AHU units with VFD capacity, but not integrate into BAS
items.text:
Although the AHU units are in generally good mechanical condition, the building is not equipped with a centralized Building Automation System (BAS) to coordinate AHU operation with the rest of the mechanical systems.

Integration of the existing VFD-controlled AHU units into a BAS would enable improved scheduling, supply air temperature reset, demand-based ventilation, and alarm monitoring. These enhancements would improve overall energy performance, operational oversight, and long-term system reliability.

items.title: Rooftop MUA
items.text: Ventilation for the building is provided by One (1)make-up air (MUA) units, located in roof top, serving corridors and other public areas.

items.title: Exhaust Only System
items.text: Ventilation is provided by centralized exhaust fans without dedicated supply air units

items.title: VFD+Gas Fire+DX Cooling
items.text:
The units are equipped with supply fans with variable frequency drives (VFDs), integral gas-fired heating burners, and DX cooling sections. The VFD, gas-fired heating burner, and DX Cooling coil were observed to be in fair to good condition.

Equipment appeared to be functioning as intended during the site walkthrough, with no visible signs of mechanical distress.

items.title: VFD+Gas Fire+Air Cooled Chiller
items.text:
The units are equipped with supply fans with variable frequency drives (VFDs), integral gas-fired heating burners, and Air Cooled Chiller provide cooling capacity. The VFD, gas-fired heating burner, and air cooled chiller were observed to be in fair to good condition.

Equipment appeared to be functioning as intended during the site walkthrough, with no visible signs of mechanical distress.
